A $2$-periodic complex $(M,N,\varphi,\psi)$ over $R$ consists of maps $\varphi:M\to N$ and $\psi:N\to M$ with $\psi\varphi=0=\varphi\psi$. Its two cohomology modules are $H^0=\ker\varphi/\operatorname{im}\psi$ and $H^1=\ker\psi/\operatorname{im}\varphi$. When both have finite length, $e_R(M,N,\varphi,\psi)=\operatorname{length}_R H^0-\operatorname{length}_R H^1$. A $(2,1)$-periodic complex $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ is the special case $M=N$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $f : (M, \varphi, \psi) \to (M', \varphi', \psi')$
be a map of $(2, 1)$-periodic complexes whose cohomology modules
have finite length. If $\Ker(f)$ and $\Coker(f)$ have finite length,
then $e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) = e_R(M', \varphi', \psi')$.
